The total surface area of the original cube is $6$ square feet. When the cube is cut into four pieces, three cross-sections are created, each with an area of $1$ square foot. This adds $6$ square feet of surface area, bringing the total surface area of the four pieces to $12$ square feet.

When the pieces are glued together as shown in the second diagram (A-B-C-D), they are joined at the cross-sections. Each joint hides $2$ square feet of surface area (the area of the contact face on each piece). There are three such joints (A-B, B-C, and C-D).

The total reduction in surface area is $3 \times 2 = 6$ square feet.
Therefore, the total surface area of the new solid is:
$$12 - 6 = 6 \text{ square feet}$$

A: 6
